feature: Current A/324 edition, reference adoption and informative national material

ATSC.value: Current published standard (14 April 2026). The 2025-07 and 2026-04 releases update references following the 2025-04 technical text. The revision approved 12 August 2026 is a Candidate Standard, not the current final baseline.
ATSC.req: published technical baseline; candidate revision separate

TTA.clause: Part 4 §2 and Appendix I-2 opening; monitoring §§5–6
TTA.value: Part 4 cites the January 2020 A/324 candidate revision and translates DSTP/ALPTP into Appendix I-2, explicitly not part of the standard. It does not reproduce the complete scheduler/CTP/STLTP/transmitter clauses. Separate national monitoring and TxID/BSID guidelines exist.
TTA.req: I-2 informative, not normative/mandatory; related national guidelines separate

SBTVD.clause: Ato §4.1; OG-02 Annex C and bibliography [12]
SBTVD.value: Ato requires transmitter/retransmitter conformity with A/324:2025-07. OG-02 separately references A/324:2024-04 for CTP-based STL; it labels itself non-normative. Full ABNT profile not fully verified.

difference: Korean informative excerpts and related operating/monitoring guidance do not constitute complete normative adoption of current A/324. Brazil’s Ato cites a technically aligned older release, while the public guideline cites a different edition.
impact: Document/reference alignment does not establish actual gateway/exciter interoperability, vendor conformance or deployed STL behavior.

TTA.text: 2020-CS DSTP/ALPTP excerpts are informative; separate monitoring and identification guidelines provide related coverage.

SBTVD.text: A/324:2025-07 incorporation verified; full national profile and equipment conformity not verified.

evidence.label: A/324 Candidate Revision — status, not final baseline
TTA Part 4 — Appendix I-2 opening, PDF p.372

recommendation: Correct the Korean mandatory labels, retain the separate OG reference edition and track the 2026 Candidate Standard without replacing the final baseline.

feature: DSTP/ALPTP and the DSMapping configuration-version differences

ATSC.value: RTP-based DSTP and ALPTP include packet metadata and EA wake-up control. Current DSMapping uses the 2021 namespace, DSMapping-1.0-20210512.xsd and a JSON-schema alternative; configuration is control-plane information outside normal DSTP/ALPTP/STLTP data paths.
ATSC.req: normative definitions for the interfaces used

TTA.value: Informative 2020-CS-derived excerpts retain a 2016 namespace and DSMapping-1.0-2019mmdd.xsd placeholder; the configuration text contains broken cross-references and no JSON alternative. Basic tunnel and ALPTP single-PLP-stream rules correspond in the inspected passages.
TTA.req: informative appendix, explicitly not part of the standard

SBTVD.doc: A/324:2025-07 by Ato reference · SBTVD OG-02
SBTVD.clause: Ato §4.1; OG-02 Annex C references A/324:2024-04
SBTVD.value: Ato incorporates the older ATSC release for transmitter equipment; the guideline confirms CTP-based STL recommendations using its own cited edition. Complete ABNT normative mapping unverified.

difference: Basic protocol concepts correspond, but the Korean DSMapping namespace/schema and available configuration forms differ from the current standard. The appendix’s informative status is a separate difference.
impact: Configuration/schema interoperability must be checked explicitly. Gateway-side location does not make an unreviewed delta automatically low impact.

TTA.text: Confirmed DSMapping edition/configuration differences and informative appendix status.

SBTVD.text: ATSC incorporation confirmed; complete national profile and actual interface behavior not verified.

evidence.label: Official A/324 version history — 2021 DSMapping Clarification

recommendation: Use a partial-match verdict, remove Korean mandatory labels and itemize the DSMapping changes before claiming current-protocol equivalence.

feature: STLTP/CTP, transmitter timing and related Korean monitoring provisions

ATSC.clause: §5 scheduler/BGW; §6 CTP; §9 STLTP; §10 transmitter requirements; Annex F
ATSC.value: Defines scheduler/management, common tunneling, STL transport and transmitter timing/operation. Mode-specific constraints apply; support and conformance must be interpreted within the implemented interface and transmission mode.
ATSC.req: normative interface and transmitter provisions within scope

TTA.page: Part 4 p.2; monitoring pp.2–6; national-rule excerpt
TTA.value: No complete translation of A/324 §§5,6,9,10 was found in Part 4. However, 0154/R1 specifies STLTP monitoring, synchronized measurement time, network_delay_now=Device_System_Time−Packet_Release_Time, Max_Delay/drop/FEC checks. The cited rule separately specifies SFN frequency tolerance ±2.1 Hz.
TTA.req: full A/324 adoption not identified in Part 4; monitoring guideline and RF tolerance separate

SBTVD.doc: A/324:2025-07 by Ato reference · SBTVD OG-02 · SBTVD OG-01 (Sep 2026)
SBTVD.clause: Ato §§4.1, 5.1.1; OG-02 Annex C; OG-01 §5.3 and Annex C §4
SBTVD.page: Ato web clauses; OG-02 p.7; OG-01 pp.6, 38–39
SBTVD.value: Ato applies referenced ATSC transmitter requirements to conformity assessment of transmitters/retransmitters. OG-02 describes CTP-based STL using A/324:2024-04. This does not prove every interface has been independently tested. OG-01 §5.3 states ±0.5 Hz (A/324:2025-07 item 10.3.1); its September 2026 Annex C §4, copied from Anatel rules, keeps ±0.5 Hz for SFN transmitters and allows ±500 Hz (≤100 W) or ±1 Hz (>100 W) for non-SFN transmitters.
SBTVD.req: transmitter conformity rule; non-normative operating guideline

difference: Part 4 does not provide a complete current A/324 adoption. It is incorrect to generalize this to absence of all Korean STL/timing guidance: a separate monitoring standard contains related provisions. For SFN operation, Brazil’s public guidance states ±0.5 Hz, tighter than the ±2.1 Hz in the cited Korean rule.
impact: Formal reference adoption, monitoring methods and actual link interoperability are distinct. No live STLTP, synchronization or equipment conformance was tested.
recommendation: Add 0154/R1 to the A/324 mapping and scope any absence claim to the reviewed Part 4 clauses. A future adoption proposal should identify the exact uncovered current clauses.

TTA.text: Complete interface adoption not identified in Part 4; national STLTP monitoring/timing guidance exists.

SBTVD.text: Regulatory incorporation verified; complete national profile and implementation/conformity test results remain unverified.

feature: TxID RF mechanism, national operation and per-stream BSID assignment

ATSC.clause: A/322 Annex N; A/324 §5 transmitter controls; A/322 L1D_bsid; A/331 SLT@bsid
ATSC.page: A/322 pp.253–256 and §9.3.1; A/331 SLT definition
ATSC.value: TxID uses a Gold-code DSBSS watermark in the first preamble symbol and defined injection levels. BSID identifies a broadcast stream; RF L1D_bsid and SLT@bsid belong to different signaling layers and must be interpreted with their version/scope rules.
ATSC.req: TxID optional in ATSC; selected-mode and signaling constraints apply

TTA.clause: Part 4 Appendix I-1.12; TTAR §§5–7, Table 5-1 and Appendix II
TTA.value: TTAR provides four-digit TxID allocation, optional activation and BGW/STL or manual control. Its ≥−24 dB recommendation is scoped to detection in SFN overlap areas and must be read with mode-specific maximum-level recommendations and AWGN test conditions. BSID applies per broadcast stream, follows the DTV TSID plan and requires SLT@bsid=L1D_bsid; L1D_bsid is active from L1D_version=1. Part 4 I-1 is explicitly not part of the standard.
TTA.req: TxID optional operating guideline; per-stream BSID assignment/equality prescribed in the guideline; appendix status separate

SBTVD.doc: Decreto 12.595/2025 · Ato 2.705/2026 · SBTVD OG-01 · SBTVD OG-02 (Sep 2026)
SBTVD.clause: Decreto Art.3 III; Ato §4.1; OG-01 §§2,5.6; OG-02 Annex A.3–A.4
SBTVD.value: Decreto includes TxID in TV 3.0. OG-01 discusses 13-bit identifiers, per-polarization choices and a 24 dB injection recommendation, and states TxID use is mandatory while the document itself is non-normative; its September 2026 §2 says each transmitter’s value “should” (previously “shall”) be uniquely assigned per RF channel. OG-02 (Sep 2026) Annex A.3–A.4 recommends deriving the BSID from the Anatel call sign (third letter A/B/P/Q/T → 0–4, then the three digits; 0–4999 recommended, 5000–65535 reserved), assigning txid_address sequentially from 0001 in each network and identifying a station by L1D_bsid plus txid_address; it cites A/322:2026-06 Annex N for up to 8,191 transmitters. This is an assignment method; a station-by-station allocation plan was not identified in the reviewed sources; publication elsewhere is not ruled out.
SBTVD.req: system adoption by decree; transmitter rule; OG-01 statements non-normative; full ABNT operation profile unverified

difference: The underlying TxID technology is shared, while national operation and allocation differ. A technical report’s assignment rules, a decree’s system-level adoption and a guideline’s mandatory wording have different authority. Brazil’s public BSID rule is station-based (derived from the call sign), whereas the Korean guideline assigns BSID per broadcast stream following the DTV TSID plan.
impact: Use of a different BSID per stream and correct L1/SLT consistency are distinct from transmitter identification. Actual TxID injection, allocation compliance and received identifiers were not tested.

TTA.text: Mechanism corresponds; national optional operation, assignment guidance, appendix status and version conditions are additional distinctions.

SBTVD.text: Decree and public operating guidance, including the OG-02 BSID/TxID assignment method, verified; normative ABNT operation/assignment details not fully verified.

evidence.label: Current A/322 — Annex N and L1D_bsid

recommendation: Keep −24 dB and BSID statements scoped to their source conditions; add the A/331 source for SLT and record allocation-plan searches as not-found-in-reviewed-sources rather than unpublished.
